elements.id-string-10: We discuss the natural range of the Unambiguous-SAT problem with respect to the number of clauses.
elements.id-string-11: We prove that for a given Boolean formula in precise conjunctive normal form with $n$ variables, there exist functions $f(n)$ and $g(n)$ such that if the number of clauses is greater than $f(n)$ then the formula does not have a satisfying truth assignment and if the number of clauses is greater than $g(n)$ then the formula either has a unique satisfying truth assignment or no satisfying truth assignment.
elements.id-string-12: The interval between functions $f(n)$ and $g(n)$ is the \emph{natural range} of the ${Unambiguous-SAT}$ problem.
elements.id-string-13: We also provide several counting rules and an algorithm that determine the unsatisfiability of some formulas in polynomial time.
elements.id-string-17: The study of restricted non-deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines  was introduced in \cite{V76} with the complexity class {\bf UP}.
elements.id-string-18: This complexity class possesses what is called a promise problem rather than a complete problem.
elements.id-string-19: The promise problem for {\bf UP} is called ${Unambiguous-SAT}$.
elements.id-string-20: It asks the question that given a Boolean formula in Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF) that is promised to have a unique satisfying truth assignment or none, does it have a unique satisfying truth assignment?
elements.id-string-21: This is a totally different problem than the ${Unique-SAT}$ problem, which is a complete problem for complexity class {\bf US} that was defined in \cite{BG82}.
elements.id-string-22: The ${Unique-SAT}$ problem asks the question that given a Boolean formula in CNF, is it true that it has a unique satisfying truth assignment?
elements.id-string-23: The isolation lemma in \cite{VV86} showed that {\bf NP} $\subseteq$ {\bf RP }$^{Unambiguous-SAT}$, where {\bf RP} is the randomized polynomial time that was defined in \cite{G77}.
elements.id-string-24: The consequence of this was that if ${Unambiguous-SAT}$ could be solved in polynomial time then {\bf RP} = {\bf NP}.\footnote{More thorough explanation of complexity classes and the relationships between them can be found in \cite{HO02}.\nocite{CP18}}
elements.id-string-25: In this paper, we define what we call the precise conjunctive normal form (PCNF).
elements.id-string-26: We show the total number of different clauses you can have for Boolean formulas in PCNF with $n$ variables.
elements.id-string-27: We also explain a way to go from Boolean formulas in CNF to Boolean formulas in PCNF in polynomial time.
elements.id-string-28: We then prove the following two functions with respect to the total number of clauses for Boolean formulas in PCNF with $n$ variables:
elements.id-string-29: 1) The \underline{final point of satisfiability} denoted by function $f(n)$, such that if there are more than $f(n)$ many clauses then the given Boolean formula in PCNF will have no satisfying truth assignment.
elements.id-string-30: 2) The \underline{last point of double satisfiability} denoted by function $g(n)$, such that if there are more than $g(n)$ many clauses the given Boolean formula in PCNF will either have a unique satisfying truth assignment or no satisfying truth assignment.
elements.id-string-31: The \emph{natural range} of the ${Unambiguous-SAT}$ problem lies between these two points for Boolean formulas in PCNF.
elements.id-string-32: We then provide several additional functions that determine the unsatisfiability of a given Boolean formula in PCNF by counting the number of literals and variables.
elements.id-string-33: We then present a polynomial time algorithm that determines the unsatisfiability of some Boolean formulas in PCNF by counting the number of clauses.
elements.id-string-35: A Boolean formula consists of one or more literals $\{l_{1}, l_{2}, l_{3}, ...\}$ that are separated by conjunction ($\wedge$) and/or disjunction ($\vee$) operators.
elements.id-string-36: A literal could be a variable ($a$) or its complement ($\sim a$), when the negation ($\sim$) operator is used, and it could be assigned the value True or False.
elements.id-string-37: A Boolean formula is said to be satisfiable if some truth assignment to its variables makes the Boolean formula evaluate to True.
elements.id-string-38: On the other hand, a Boolean formula is said to be unsatisfiable if all possible combinations of truth assignments to its variables makes the Boolean formula evaluate to False.

elements.id-string-49: A Boolean formula in Precise Conjunctive Normal Form (PCNF) consists of conjunction of unique clauses, where the clauses are a disjunction of unique literals and do not contain both the variable and its complement.
